turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not the only person to feel sympathy for Mr. Wickham, I believe. His faults have been excused, and his misrepresentations encouraged.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am surprised, Miss Bennet, to find you so prejudiced against my character. Your judgment is not easily swayed, I see.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not surprised, sir, by your misconceptions of my character. You have always been generous in your opinions of others.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your judgement is certainly not one I am accustomed to earning, Miss Bennet. I must confess, however, that my understanding of your character has been as flawed as your perception of mine.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your past actions have left me with little reason to believe in your regard for my character. It is hard to reconcile your former behavior with your present sentiments.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I acknowledge the justice of your sentiments, Miss Bennet. My actions have been such as to merit your ill opinion.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, I am not inclined to soften my opinion of you, despite your confession. Your past treatment of me and my family cannot be easily forgiven.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am aware of the difficulty of earning your trust, Elizabeth. My efforts to amend my ways are the only assurance I can offer.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your words ring true, but actions speak louder than words. I will not forget the past, but I will observe your future conduct.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand the weight of your words, Elizabeth. My future conduct will indeed be the measure of my sincerity.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I hope, Mr. Darcy, that your actions will be worthy of your words. Until then, I must reserve my judgment.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I will strive to earn your trust, Elizabeth. My actions will be my testament.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I see, Mr. Darcy. Let us hope for the best, then.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall do everything in my power to prove myself to you, Miss Elizabeth. Farewell, for now.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Goodbye, Mr. Darcy. I shall await the changes in your character with interest.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Elizabeth, I am earnest in my intentions and hope for the opportunity to demonstrate my sincerity.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, I must say I am taken aback by your declaration. I have always held you in the highest regard for your wealth and status, but I find your character far less commendable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am aware of your opinion of me, Miss Elizabeth. Yet, I cannot help but feel that my character is more complex than you perceive.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your character may be complex, Mr. Darcy, but the actions which have been reported to me paint a clear picture of a man who is proud and disdainful of those he deems inferior. I cannot overlook the pain you have caused.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Elizabeth, I have indeed been guilty of pride and prejudice. However, I must assert that my actions have been guided by a misguided sense of duty and a desire to protect those I hold dear.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: His misfortunes! yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
